title: Casper and the Extraction
premise: Ulyana Quintana, a peace-delegation interpreter, receives a meeting invitation from her handler—sent the day after his funeral. Following it pulls her into Casper, a deniable extraction network that trained her and now needs her silence more than her skills. As she decodes her dead handler's breadcrumbs, she discovers the delegation's collapse was engineered to bury evidence of Casper's worst operation. To survive, she must burn the network that made her, choosing love for a compromised colleague over the duty that kept her invisible. The book ends with Ulyana testifying off the record to a journalist, trading justice outside the law for a life she can finally own.
about_author: Jude Coldharbour is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in contested border regions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people whose paperwork matters more than their names.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At her handler Marek's sparsely attended funeral, her phone buzzes: a calendar invite from his account, tomorrow, 6 a.m., an abandoned customs house. She tells herself it's a phishing trap—but packs a go-bag anyway. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion as ten years of careful invisibility begin to feel like someone else's design.

chapters.title: Six A.M.
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She keeps the meeting; no one comes, but a dead-drop locker holds Marek's notebook and a burner phone preloaded with one contact: CASPER. Inside the notebook, her own recruitment file—redacted in ways that don't match official records. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing her past has been edited by hands she never saw.

chapters.title: The Delegation That Fails
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with delegation security chief Tomas Reyes. Peace talks open in Geneva amid leaks Ulyana is ordered to soften in translation. She notices her rendered interpretations are being altered upstream—and that Marek flagged the same pattern weeks before he died. Emotional beat: professional dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ulyana's POV. Ten years earlier: her recruitment into Casper's interpreter pipeline, the training that taught her to disappear inside other people's sentences. Present-day intercut: she tests the burner phone and gets a reply in Marek's phrasing habits. Emotional beat: nostalgia weaponized—the network knew exactly who she'd become.

chapters.title: A Colleague Compromised
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Reyes discovers financial anomalies pointing at his own deputy and realizes he's being set up as the fall guy for the talks' collapse. He approaches Ulyana—not trusting her, needing her languages. Emotional beat: two guarded professionals recognizing each other's cages.

chapters.title: Dead Handler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Decoding Marek's notebook: dates, wire transfers, and a recurring codename—LANTERN—attached to an operation in Vukovar twelve years ago. The delegation's failure isn't incompetence; it's cover. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing fear; the dead man left her a ledger, not a message.

chapters.title: The Tail
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Both are followed after a covert meeting; Tomas burns a surveillance team to buy Ulyana an exit, revealing training he claims to have forgotten. Emotional beat: attraction kindling under adrenaline, each suspecting the other of being the trap.

chapters.title: What LANTERN Buried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She locates a retired Casper quartermaster in Trieste who confirms LANTERN: a staged massacre used to justify an intervention, its witnesses extracted or erased. Her translation work softened the aftermath. Emotional beat: guilt arriving late and total—she was the network's voice.

chapters.title: Orders to Stand Down
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His agency orders him home and seizes his credentials; the talks collapse on schedule. He chooses to stay dark and help Ulyana instead of obeying. Emotional beat: duty cracking—love against duty becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Second Invitation
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The burner summons her to a safehouse where a living Casper officer, Director Ilse Brandt, offers amnesty for silence and a promotion for loyalty—while making clear what happened to Marek. Emotional beat: terror wearing a friendly face; the offer is a countdown.

chapters.title: Marek's Last Cut
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Forensics on Marek's death point to a staged suicide by a Casper cleaner codenamed VESSEL. Tomas traces VESSEL's movements toward Ulyana. Emotional beat: protective urgency outrunning caution.

chapters.title: Interpreting the Enemy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using her linguistic access, she infiltrates a Casper comms relay and copies the LANTERN archive—including orders bearing Brandt's signature. Emotional beat: empowerment with teeth; her invisibility becomes the perfect camouflage.

chapters.title: VESSEL
chapters.summary: Split POV. The cleaner corners them in a Zurich parking structure; Tomas takes a knife wound shielding Ulyana before she turns VESSEL's own tradecraft against him and escapes with the archive intact. Emotional beat: first blood—survival has a price and they've started paying it.

chapters.title: Safehouse Confessions
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. While Tomas's wound festers, they trade truths: his buried service record, her recruitment, the years each spent performing loyalty. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in confinement; love admitted quietly, almost apologetically.

chapters.title: The Network Fights Back
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Casper leaks doctored files naming Ulyana a double agent; her bank accounts freeze, her sister in Manila is contacted by 'welfare officers.' Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal—the network attacks everything soft in her.

chapters.title: Sister's Keeper
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A brutal side trip to extract her sister from Casper's leverage, using a forged diplomatic corridor only an interpreter could build. Emotional beat: fury refined into resolve; she stops asking permission from any system.

chapters.title: Brandt's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Cross-referencing the archive, she finds LANTERN's surviving witness alive in a Baltic care facility—and realizes Brandt plans a second, larger operation timed to the post-collapse vacuum. Emotional beat: stakes escalate from vindication to prevention.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Split POV. They extract the witness through a snowbound port while Casper closes every legal channel; Tomas sacrifices his last official ally to hold the perimeter. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph—justice assembled entirely outside the law.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She triggers a coordinated release: archive to three journalists, evidence to two prosecutors, and a poisoned copy into Casper's own servers that unravels their finances. Emotional beat: catharsis with tremors—burning it down means burning her old self too.

chapters.title: Ilse Brandt, Cornered
chapters.summary: Climax, split POV. Confrontation at a decommissioned airfield where Brandt attempts the second operation's launch and offers Ulyana Marek's old job one final time. Ulyana refuses in five languages; Brandt is arrested by the one honest prosecutor still standing. Emotional beat: the invitation finally declined.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Off the record, she gives a journalist everything, accepting that formal justice will be partial and her name will stay dirty. Tomas, cleared but changed, asks what she'll do now. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into authorship of her own story.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ulyana's POV. Months later: teaching interpretation to refugees, her sister nearby, Tomas learning to cook badly in her kitchen. A new invitation arrives from an unknown sender; she deletes it without opening. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace—invisibility traded for a life seen.
